title: Trying to make a kinetic novel/cohab sim on godot 4 with some mouse based minigames, which animation rigging software after disecting body parts? godot or loongbones or spine2d pro
author: rvshankar2712
selftext:
For my first iteration I just want to move the characters limbs, get a screenshot of the changed arm position and then use it as static image asset after tweaking reaction in inpaint edit/upscaling. 

I am able to generate beautiful images on newer image models like moss-sft (moved away from older wai illustrious model) but editing the character arms, without sacrificing consistency is proving to be a headache. It always changes something either the background, degrades the image, character clothing like sleeve appearance etc. I have tried control net, reference image etc but the subtle change is definitely noticeable and I have convinced myself to put in some actual effort into understanding paper doll animation aka rigging 

I have locked in 90% of the story/script/dialogue, I learnt how to use comfy ui image generation, some mid level workflows that automatically fix artifcats, hand detailer, facial details etc, learnt how to create custom character lora. Plan to use dialogic 2 and vibecode the stat management/minigame after learning basics of gdscript, prompt AI to explain every single line/logic so I dont waste my own time asking for debugging help from others

TLDR: Which software to change limb/body static 2d character images? Live2d, spine2d, loongbones, godot 4 skeletal node, blender etc.   
  
Would be nice if the characters appear breathing and I would need something called mesh deformation which is said to be hard on godot 4 but for now just movement of character limbs in standing/sitting position is a reasonable start for a total novice like me.

Thanks for the help
